name: MonarchLineChart
title: LineChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts: Chart with LineMark (series per run of values), AreaMark(x:yStart:yEnd:series:) for the area variant, PointMark for lone and inspected points, RuleMark for reference lines and the crosshair, chartXSelection(value:) for touch inspection, inside MonarchChartFrame (accessibilityChartDescriptor and View as table)
summary: A line or area chart for trends over time or ordered categories, with several series, gaps, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: To show how one or more measures change over days, weeks or months (traffic, sign-ups, revenue, latency), to compare a period with the previous one (a dashed series), or to show a trend against a target (a reference line).
whenNotToUse: To compare unordered categories, use a bar chart or MonarchBarList. For a small trend in a table cell or a card, use MonarchSparkline. For two measures in different units, draw two charts and share activeIndex instead of a second axis.

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, a heading in the frame and the name VoiceOver reads.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values, in order. Points are spaced by time, so uneven dates show.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values, in order, already localised. Points are spaced evenly.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, each with a key, a label, one value per x value (nil is a gap), an optional colour slot and isDashed.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title: the period, the unit or the question it answers.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table. Built in: "Date" or "Category".

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure, for the data table and VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed horizontal lines with a label and value: targets, baselines, service levels.

options.name: variant
options.description: line, or area: the line with a soft fill down to the baseline.

options.name: curve
options.description: linear, or monotone: smooth without overshooting the data.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error, passed to the frame. A ready chart without x values is empty.

options.name: includesZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero. Turn it off for values far from zero.

options.name: valueDomain
options.description: Fixes the value axis, such as 0...100 for percentages.

options.name: showsPoints
options.description: A dot on every point. Lone points between gaps always get one.

options.name: isLegendInteractive
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected index. Bind several charts with the same x values to one value to share the crosshair.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: How dates are written in the popover and the data table (dates initialiser). Set its time zone for fixed output.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the frame's empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart: the source, the last update.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the plot, kept in every status. 240 points when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the frame's built-in strings; noValue is also the popover's text for a gap.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the popover, the table, VoiceOver and reference labels. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: default
states.description: One line per visible series in its colour slot, with axes from Swift Charts; dashed series have a dashed line.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: While the plot is touched, or activeIndex is set: a vertical crosshair, a larger point on each visible series and a popover with the x value and every visible series' value.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the value range; its legend entry is struck through; it stays in the data table.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks the line; a lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: area
states.description: Each line has a soft fill of its colour down to zero, or to the lowest value when zero is left out.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's placeholder, empty state or error with Try again, at the chart's height.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" swaps the plot for the data table.

appearance: Series use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (a sixth series and later are neutral, the subtle text colour); the area fill is the series colour at low strength. Reference lines and their labels are the muted text colour, dashed; the crosshair is the strong border colour; the popover is the raised surface with a medium shadow. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts, which draws the axes, ticks and grid and spaces date values by time; the web draws its own SVG. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection: the crosshair follows the finger and clears when it lifts, where the web keeps the last tapped point. There is no keyboard inspection, live region or generated text summary: VoiceOver gets the data through the frame's accessibility chart descriptor, whose Audio Graph describes each series. The web xScale option is the choice of initialiser (dates or categories); dates cannot be spaced evenly. The web onPointSelect (drill-in) and the frame's header actions are not offered. locale, valueFormat and xFormat are the environment locale, formatValue and dateFormat; value-axis ticks use Swift Charts' own number format. Right-to-left layout follows Swift Charts. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one element named by the title, with the data as an accessibility chart descriptor (Audio Graphs and the chart's data table in the rotor).
"View as table" shows the data table, where each row is read as the x value followed by every series and its value, "No value" for a gap. Hidden series stay in the table.
Values are read with formatValue, so VoiceOver says "410 ms" rather than "410".
The inspection popover is hidden from VoiceOver.
Series differ by their names in the legend and, where isDashed is set, by a dashed line and marker, not by colour alone.
Legend toggles are switches named by the series; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
Text in the frame, legend, popover and reference labels scales with Dynamic Type; the plot keeps its height.
edgeCases: Missing, nil and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; a series shorter than the x values ends in gaps, and extra values are dropped.
A ready chart with no x values shows the empty state.
A single series has no legend; its name is the title.
With includesZero off and no valueDomain, the area fills down to the lowest visible value.
Reference lines are part of the value range, so a target far above the data stays visible.
An activeIndex outside the x values is ignored.
Duplicate categories are separate points in the table but share one position on the axis; give unique categories.

MonarchLineChart(
    {{title}},
    dates: days,
    series: [
        MonarchLineChartSeries({{series.0.key}}, label: {{series.0.label}}, values: [{{series.0.values.0}}, {{series.0.values.1}}, {{series.0.values.2}}, {{series.0.values.3}}, {{series.0.values.4}}, {{series.0.values.5}}, {{series.0.values.6}}, {{series.0.values.7}}, {{series.0.values.8}}, {{series.0.values.9}}, {{series.0.values.10}}, {{series.0.values.11}}, {{series.0.values.12}}, {{series.0.values.13}}]),
        MonarchLineChartSeries(
            {{series.1.key}},
            label: {{series.1.label}},
            values: [{{series.1.values.0}}, {{series.1.values.1}}, {{series.1.values.2}}, {{series.1.values.3}}, {{series.1.values.4}}, {{series.1.values.5}}, {{series.1.values.6}}, {{series.1.values.7}}, {{series.1.values.8}}, {{series.1.values.9}}, {{series.1.values.10}}, {{series.1.values.11}}, {{series.1.values.12}}, {{series.1.values.13}}],

examples.code:
MonarchLineChart(
    "Sessions",
    dates: days,
    series: [
        MonarchLineChartSeries("sessions", label: "This period", values: [820, 932, 901, 934, 1290, 1330, 1320, 1180, 1250, 1400, 1380, 1460, 1510, 1490]),
        MonarchLineChartSeries(
            "previous",
            label: "Previous period",
            values: [672, 764, 739, 766, 1058, 1091, 1082, 968, 1025, 1148, 1132, 1197, 1238, 1222],
            color: .neutral,
            isDashed: true
        ),
    ],
    description: "Last 14 days against the previous 14",
    referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine(1200, label: "Target")]
)

examples.title: Area with gaps over dates
examples.code:
MonarchLineChart(
    "p95 latency",
    dates: days,
    series: [MonarchLineChartSeries("p95", label: "p95", values: [210, 220, nil, 260, 240, nil, 235])],
    variant: .area,
    curve: .monotone,
    includesZero: false,
    height: 180,
    formatValue: { "\(Int($0)) ms" }
)

examples.title: Two charts sharing one crosshair
examples.code:
VStack {
    MonarchLineChart(
        "Sessions",
        categories: weeks,
        series: [MonarchLineChartSeries("sessions", label: "Sessions", values: [820, 932, 901, 1_290])],
        activeIndex: $active,
        height: 140
    )
    MonarchLineChart(
        "Sign-ups",
        categories: weeks,
        series: [MonarchLineChartSeries("signups", label: "Sign-ups", values: [42, 51, 47, 88], color: .data2)],
        activeIndex: $active,
        height: 140
    )
}

@State private var active: Int? = 2
private let weeks = ["W1", "W2", "W3", "W4"]
